title: The East Side of the Square
sceneText:
Over against the wall on the east side of the square, a man is standing and eating.

Dark grey uniform, collar not unfastened. A young man with glasses, a paper-wrapped sandwich in one hand and a small notebook in the other. Two bites, a glance at the notebook, two more bites. He eats very quickly.

There are people all around him, stallholders calling prices, children running past. He stands there like a stone of the wrong colour.

He has seen you. He swallows what is in his mouth and crushes the paper up.

{@timothy}“The new steward at Maplegate.”

You do not remember meeting him.

{@timothy}“Kessler. Secretariat,” he says. “I went through your registration papers this Wednesday.”

choices.text: Let us sit down somewhere — my treat

effects.logEntry: You asked Kessler to sit down and talk. He did not sit.

choices.resultText:
{@timothy}“No need.” He finishes the last mouthful. “I am due back in fifteen minutes.”

He puts the balled paper in his pocket and gives you a nod before he goes.

choices.text: How did you know who I was?

effects.logEntry: You asked Kessler how he had known who you were.

choices.resultText:
{@timothy}“I know every steward in this part of the district,” he says. “A new one is easier.”

He shuts the notebook and puts it away inside his uniform.

{@timothy}“I shall be at Maplegate on the twelfth of October to check the accounts.” He pushes his glasses up. “I am telling you in advance. It is only a reminder.”

That sentence has given you six days.

choices.text: Is there anything on that document I should be watching?

effects.logEntry: You asked Kessler whether there was anything on the registration to watch.

choices.resultText:
He blinks, and thinks for a while, his eyes seeming to rest on something behind you.

{@timothy}“There is one thing.” He opens the notebook again. “The guarantee runs thirty days exactly, counted from the date of arrival.”

{@timothy}“Your date of arrival is the thirtieth of September. Which makes your thirtieth day the thirtieth of October. Not the end of the month. People get that wrong, and then discover on the last day that their status has lapsed.”

{@timothy}“Also, the line for your remuneration reads one hundred and fifty guldmark. The estate’s quarterly operating budget is sixty.” He shuts the notebook. “That is not my business. Only, if anybody asks where your wages come from, you should know the answer.”

He goes.
